reviews.author: Foodies Kerala
reviews.text:
Had a very disappointing experience with the service.

As soon as we entered, we ordered grilled chicken and garlic naan. Within 10 min grilled chicken arrived that, but the naan didn’t.

After waiting another 10–15 minutes more, we started asking the staff about the naan. Almost every staff member we approached told us it would take “2 more minutes.” They even showed us the TV screen and said, “See, they are preparing it in the kitchen.”

We waited for almost 30 minutes more. By that time, the grilled chicken had become almost cold, and we still hadn’t received the naan. We kept asking different staff members about it, and every time we were given the same response.

Then, surprisingly, the person who had taken our order came and told us that the garlic naan still hadn’t been prepared in the kitchen and that he wasn’t sure why. He said we could either cancel the order or order something else.

What was even more disappointing was his attitude. Instead of properly explaining the situation or apologising, he was extremely arrogant and seemed completely unconcerned about the inconvenience caused. His attitude was literally like, “Cancel the order and leave.”

The other staff members did apologise, which I appreciate. I could even see them going to the person who took our order and telling him about the situation, but his attitude was still as if it didn’t matter that we had cancelled.

In the end, we simply ate the grilled chicken, which had already become almost cold, and left the restaurant without having a proper meal.

Very poor service and communication. because customers shouldn’t have to repeatedly ask about an order for 30 minutes, receive misleading updates, and then be told that the item wasn’t even being prepared.

reviews.author: Karan bisht
reviews.text:
I recently visited Empire Restaurant for dinner, and overall it was a satisfying experience with a mix of positives and a few small areas for improvement.
Starting with the ambience, the restaurant has a clean and modern setup with comfortable seating. The lighting and décor give a casual yet slightly premium feel, making it suitable for both family dinners and outings with friends. The place was quite busy, which is always a good sign of popularity.
Coming to the food, we ordered a variety of dishes including Pepper Chicken Masala, Butter Naan, Tandoori Roti, Paneer Tikka Masala, Curd Rice, and Tandoori Chicken.
The Pepper Chicken Masala was flavorful with a good balance of spices, though slightly on the milder side if you prefer strong heat.
Butter Naan and Tandoori Roti were fresh, soft, and well-cooked—perfect to pair with the gravies.
The Paneer Tikka Masala stood out with its creamy texture and rich taste.
Tandoori Chicken was nicely grilled and juicy, though it could have had a bit more smoky flavor.
Curd Rice was simple, comforting, and a good way to balance the meal.
The portion sizes were decent, making it a good value-for-money option, especially for groups. The total bill came to around ₹1385, which felt reasonable considering the quantity and variety ordered.
In terms of service, the staff were polite and fairly attentive, even during peak hours. However, the service speed could be slightly improved as we experienced a bit of waiting time between dishes.
One thing worth mentioning is the overall consistency.Empire is known for delivering reliable taste, and this visit lived up to that expectation.
Final verdict:
A great place for a hearty North Indian meal with good portions and reasonable pricing. While there is slight room for improvement in service speed and flavor intensity, the overall experience is definitely worth it.

reviews.author: Nayana Hd
reviews.text:
We encountered several severe lapses in service and professionalism that we feel must be addressed:

Negligent Service: Upon arrival, we had to request the menu three times. Alarmingly, a manager in a blazer watched this happen but chose to wait for a waiter rather than taking the initiative to assist us. Furthermore, after our food arrived, we had to ask for basic dining plates twice.

Bait-and-Switch Pricing: We ordered the Chicken Shawarma explicitly listed on the menu for ₹90 each, but we were served a different version and charged a higher price. Similarly, we ordered two glasses of grape juice (listed at approximately ₹180 per glass), but staff brought a full bottle instead and inflated the bill. Upselling is understandable, but forcing unrequested, higher-priced items onto guests is financially unethical.

Kitchen Mismanagement: We were informed that the Biryani would take 30 minutes to prepare. We willingly agreed to wait for a fresh dish, only to be served cold Biryani just 5 minutes later.

Unwelcoming Atmosphere: Within 5 minutes of serving the cold Biryani, the staff placed finger bowls on our table. This felt like a deliberate and incredibly rude attempt to rush us out of the restaurant, making us feel thoroughly unwelcome.

Crowd management should never come at the expense of basic hospitality, and guests should never be manipulated into paying more than the menu price. Your supervisory staff in blazers need to take hands-on initiative to ensure a positive guest experience rather than standing by passively.

I strongly recommend immediate, comprehensive retraining for both your floor and management staff regarding basic hospitality etiquette, order accuracy, and honest billing practices. I look forward to your prompt response detailing how you intend to rectify these systemic issues

reviews.author: Kanika kanwal
reviews.text:
We visited the restaurant for grilled chicken, and the experience was delightful from the start. The ambiance was inviting, and our order included grilled chicken, Mutton Special, Empire Special Paratha, and Mint Lime Soda.

The grilled chicken was incredibly juicy and flavourful, with the chutney adding an extra layer of taste. Mayonnaise is available if desired, but it’s not necessary. The Mutton Special was a revelation, featuring a unique South Indian touch that made it both tender and spicy. It was unlike anything I’ve tasted before. The Empire Special Paratha was a perfect match, offering a crispy, warm, and flavourful complement to the mutton. The Mint Lime Soda was refreshing and aided digestion, with its minty and light taste.

A special mention goes to the staff, who were exceptionally polite and attentive. They kindly recommended dishes and ensured we had everything we needed throughout our meal. Their efforts made our dining experience at Empire Restaurant truly memorable. Thank you!

reviews.author: Muhammad Shafeer
reviews.text:
Easily the best spot on Church Street for a satisfying meal.
​Food (5/5): The flavors are consistently amazing. The Empire Special Chicken Kebab is a classic and was cooked to perfection—crispy on the outside and juicy inside. Their Ghee Rice paired with Dal or Butter Chicken is a must-try combination. Even with the heavy rush, the food quality remains top-notch.
​Service (5/5): Despite being one of the busiest outlets in Bangalore, the staff is incredibly quick and attentive. My order arrived much faster than expected.
​Value (5/5): The rates are very reasonable considering the generous portions and the prime location. It’s the perfect place for a high-quality meal that doesn't break the bank.
​Whether you're looking for a quick bite or a full dinner, this place never disappoints. A 10/10 experience!"

reviews.author: Navish P
reviews.text:
Avoid the hype! We visited Empire Hotel based on a recommendation, and even the person who suggested it was thoroughly disappointed. While the location is unbeatable, the food and service were a total disaster.
We started with Gobi Manchurian, crispy shrimps, and chicken tandoori. Only the Gobi was remotely edible; the rest was a letdown. Things went downhill from there. We ordered veg fried rice, mutton biryani, and a mix of butter rotis and naans. The fried rice was served bone-dry—we had to wait 15 minutes just for a basic sauce. The rotis were so hard they were essentially papads, and the butter naans were soggy and rubbery. As for the curries (including the Hyderabad style), they were far below average and lacked any real flavor.
Service was equally lackluster, making the overall experience incredibly frustrating. It seems like this place is riding on a reputation from decades ago that no longer exists. I would honestly rather stay hungry or pay double to travel elsewhere than eat here again. Don’t listen to the old Bangalore nostalgia; this place is overhyped and under-delivers. Save your money and your appetite—stay away!

reviews.author: Saheer T
reviews.text:
I recently visited the Empire Restaurant on Church Street, and my experience was nothing short of delightful. The restaurant has always been known for its consistency and charm, and this visit once again reaffirmed why it remains one of my preferred dining destinations in the city.

The highlight of my meal was the grilled chicken paired with their signature ghee rice. The chicken was cooked to perfection—tender, juicy, and seasoned with just the right balance of spices that brought out an authentic and robust flavor. The smokiness of the grill added an irresistible depth that complemented the richness of the dish beautifully. Alongside, the ghee rice was fragrant, fluffy, and carried that subtle buttery aroma which paired wonderfully with the chicken. Together, the combination created a truly satisfying and memorable meal.

Beyond the food, what stood out was the warm and welcoming atmosphere. From the moment I stepped in, I felt an immediate sense of comfort. The team managed to strike the perfect balance between attentiveness and giving guests their space, which made the dining experience smooth and enjoyable. Every detail, from the presentation of dishes to the timely service, reflected a commitment to quality and customer satisfaction.

This was not my first visit to the Empire, what impresses me most is the consistency they maintain. Each time, the food arrives with the same freshness and flavor, and the dining experience feels special. It’s rare to find a place that can deliver such reliable excellence in both cuisine and service.

Empire on Church Street continues to shine as a dependable destination for a hearty meal. The grilled chicken and ghee rice alone are worth returning for, and I look forward to many more visits in the future.

reviews.author: Subiksha R
reviews.text:
A group of three of us went here for lunch after shopping on a Sunday afternoon. As expected, the place was very crowded over the weekend, and we waited about 20 minutes to get a table.

Since we were quite hungry, we ordered paneer kebab (4/5), chicken kebab (4/5), wheat parotta, and nool parotta. The parottas are served in two pieces.

One of the best things here is that gravies are available in 1/4, 1/2, and full portions, which allows you to try multiple varieties without over-ordering.

Overall, the food was tasty and delicious, and the experience was worth it😄

reviews.author: Shashank Ravi
reviews.text:
I am writing this to express my deep disappointment with the service I experienced at Empire Restaurant MG Road
. Unfortunately, it was one of the worst dining experiences I have ever had.

From the moment I entered, the staff showed a complete lack of interest in serving customers. There was no proper greeting, and we were made to wait unnecessarily despite the restaurant not being very crowded. The staff appeared untrained, rude, and careless, responding to queries with irritation rather than courtesy.

reviews.author: Pranit
reviews.text: The food's great. If you're a non veg it's a paradise, for veg there are lot less options. Though the prices are high the quality fits it. Try the butter chicken , it's great , other dishes are also very good.

reviews.author: Veena H
reviews.text: Very worst experience from managerial staff. First of all the manager was of an attitude such that we are eating at his expense! I ordered few things and then added one more, but since they were making a delayed delivery of the food I cancelled it and asked for the bill, the manager who took the order was so rude and arrogant. Then while printing the bill I reassured that the food I cancelled is not added in the bill, since I had asked them in addition about that and since they specifically mentioned the number, I didn't check it in the bill and paid. After payment I got to see that they had included the food that I cancelled. I asked them about it and then the only solution from the management was to add that additional amount to the dept of the guy who was serving us. They were not ready to make the manager the culprit! Why that poor guy has to take the responsibility, only because I was quite busy I didn't argue about it and left the place. I don't know whether it's a plan from them to make me feel this way leave the place or what. This is too bad, I'll never suggest anybody to go to empire restaurant even though the food is good, the service must also be good!

reviews.author: Shwetha Rao
reviews.text:
No complaints about food. We had biriyani and grilled chicken and it was absolutely amazing.

But what I really didn't like was the rude behaviour of the serving staff. He is an old man. We had some confusion about the biriyani and was just politely asking. This person started being so rude to us as if we are eating food there for free.
My rating came down to two stars solely for the serving staff's behaviour.

reviews.text: The food was pretty good. Empire special parota must try. Service too good and kind . New to the place , they will guide and suggest you the dishes .o

reviews.author: Ni D
reviews.text: This is my second disappointing experience at Empire. There was a wait-time of 15 mins,as informed prior by the counter. This time I ordered the Al faham and it was not cooked well. The meat was still pink and had a raw smell. As a customer, I do not mind waiting for a table or for the food, but the least expectation is to receive a well prepared dish. The service staff is courteous  but its all a waste if the food fails and it failed miserably.

reviews.author: Umar Ahamed
reviews.text: All are well. Foods suits better. Small thing is reduce salt a little. So happy to have it

reviews.author: Ajey Parkhi
reviews.text: This restaurant is at very prime location at Church Street in Bangalore. Restaurant has the old touch and menu is not unnecessarily large. Specific dishes and they taste good. What makes this restaurant even more special is the staff there. All staff is prompt to serve you, always smiling and have customer service oriented attitude. We were served by waiter named Lucky and we got best service from him. Overall an enjoyable dinner. Their non veg dishes have simple but distinct taste and Biryani looked nice but it was sold out by the time we ordered.. for dessert lovers, do try the Gadbad. Its quite close to the authentic one you usually get at coastal karnataka side.

reviews.author: R Nikhilesh
reviews.text:
Haven't been to rooms but the restaurant is same as all other empires
Good food and friendly staff, best part about this branch is it's location. Place is also neat and clean. Lot of place to sit and have a comfortable meal.
Ghee rice and butter chicken is the best combo you must try. All in all good experience, will keep visiting as usual again and again
